articles.title: When the Rule-Maker Runs the World Championship: Late Patches and Procedural Accountability in League of Legends
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Riot Games, which runs the League of Legends World Championship (Worlds), also changes the game shortly before each tournament. This concentration of authority raises a governance question: Who scrutinizes how the benefits and burdens of late rule changes are distributed? We examine all ten championships from 2016 to 2025, combining 1,097 games, 215 team-years, and LLM coding of 1,090 champion changes across 40 patches. articles.title: Can Power Draw Constrain Covert Compute? Limits of Analogue Verification for AI Governance
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier AI treaties or agreements on limiting computation require external verification; an external auditor must be able to confirm how much computation actually ran and that parties are adhering to the agreement. Analogue, off-chip measurements such as power draw provide an information channel for verification. It is unknown how well these analogue channels can constrain computation against an adversary who actively tries to subvert the audit. articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models increasingly mediate writing, translation, information retrieval, and education, the technological support available to a language may influence its position in contemporary social life. articles.title: Online Sign Language Interpretation System
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07872v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Walloon Region commissioned this study to improve deaf people's access to public services for the new millennium. It focuses on sign language users, about 25,000 adults in the French-speaking Community, for whom written French is close to a foreign language. The core problem is a severe shortage of interpreters: only about twenty work in French-speaking Belgium, so appointments take weeks to arrange and emergencies cannot be covered. articles.title: Personalized Recommendations Without Inducing Congestion: Mitigating Disparities in the NYC High School Match
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.08275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Algorithmic recommendations can help participants navigate large matching markets. For example, recommendations for school and college choices may reduce information frictions and disparities in access to high-performing programs. articles.title: Joint upper-bound coverage and route-choice utility: an empirical evaluation on two urban proxy tasks
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.06995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether more accurate traffic forecasts or higher uncertainty coverage improve route decisions is unclear. articles.title: Educating future engineers about LLMs: A scalable workshop
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07027v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into engineering workflows, students require hands-on experience to learn how to collaborate with them critically. This paper presents a scalable gamified workshop designed for engineering Master's students to practice human-AI collaboration in navigation planning. articles.title: WPTokens: A Dataset for Studying the Regulation of Wikipedia
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.07108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studying how Wikipedia is regulated requires knowing who adds, rewrites, moves and deletes which piece of content, when and where. WPTokens is a dataset that answers these questions over the full revision history of the French-language Wikipedia. It relies on a positional diff over two layers: a text layer made of sentences, and a node layer made of the structural elements of wikitext (templates, links, references, headings, tables, lists, etc.).
